transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I can’t think clearly or concentrate the way I used to at work, and it feels like my mind just won’t stay organized. It's gotten really hard to keep up with everything at the salon, and I'm just feeling really overwhelmed by it.

Did these concentration problems start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on gradually without one clear trigger? Have they been present most days for at least the past 6 months?

They started about two years ago when I transitioned from cosmetology school to working full-time at a busy salon and living on my own, which was a really stressful adjustment. It's definitely been happening most days for much longer than six months—it feels like it's been nearly two years of dealing with this constantly.

Along with the concentration problems, have you been feeling down most of the day or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy for at least two weeks at a time? Or does it feel more like ongoing worry and stress related to work and living on your own?

It’s definitely much more than just stress—for over a year now, I've felt deeply down and empty almost every day, like a heavy gray cloud is constantly sitting on me. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my hiking club or volunteering, and most days I just feel blank and can't bring myself to care about anything.

During this past year, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? If so, which of these have been happening most days?

Yes, I've been dealing with almost all of those most days. I have no appetite and have lost weight, and my body feels so heavy, like I'm dragging a hundred pounds just to walk or lift my arms. I also feel this constant, crushing guilt over every mistake I've ever made, and there are nights I lie in bed wishing I wouldn't wake up, or picturing stepping in front of a train.

When you feel this depressed, have you ever heard or seen things that others don’t, or become convinced of things like being guilty, ruined, or deserving punishment even when others say that isn’t true? Also, are these experiences happening only during the depression?

Yes, I hear a man's voice at the salon telling me I'm a fraud, and I'm convinced people are secretly recording me to laugh at my mistakes, which makes me feel like I've ruined everyone's life. These things started when I was already in that heavy, sad fog, but they don't only happen when I'm depressed. Last fall, even during a stretch where I felt less sad, I still heard the voice and believed I was being filmed.

Have there been times when the voice and the belief that people were recording you lasted for at least 2 weeks while you were not feeling depressed at all? During those times, were you back to your usual mood or still somewhat down?

Yes, last fall there was a stretch of a few weeks where the crushing sadness lifted and I could get through my shifts a bit better, though I still wasn't completely back to my usual self. Even during those weeks when the depression wasn't there, the man's voice and the belief that I was being recorded lasted the entire time. It was really strange because those thoughts and voices stayed even when the heavy mood was gone.

Outside of those few weeks when the voice and recording belief continued, have you spent most of the last two years depressed for the majority of the time? Or have the psychotic symptoms often happened during long periods when your mood was mostly normal?

Yes, I have spent the vast majority of the last two years feeling deeply depressed. Aside from those few brief weeks last fall when my mood lifted slightly, I have felt empty, down, and guilty almost every single day since things started going downhill at the salon.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a prolonged major depressive syndrome with psychotic symptoms, plus a clearly documented period of at least 2 weeks of hallucinations and delusional beliefs occurring when depressive symptoms were absent. Because mood episodes have been present for the majority of the illness duration, this is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, rather than major depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms.
